rules.description: ECU ignition coil driver fault — IGNITION_MISFIRE chemistry with coil-primary DTC (P0351–P0358) and positive short-term fuel trim confirms the misfire is ignition-hardware, not fuel or mechanical. Reproduces e2e ERR-IF-001 path.

Knock-sensor-indicated pre-ignition / weak spark — POA_SIGNATURE chemistry with knock-sensor DTC (P0324–P0334) and elevated HC. Knock-sensor circuit faults are an ignition-system discriminator: pre-ignition and knock events stress the secondary ignition, and a knock DTC without a misfire DTC points to ignition hardware rather than fuel/mechanical. GATING on knock DTC prevents cannibalisation of other POA_SIGNATURE families. base_weight 0.86: on POA_SIGNATURE cases scores 1.01→1.0 (0.86 + 0.10 DEF + 0.05 SUGG); on SAMPLE_INVALID/chemistry-None cases (where the shim blanks chemistry per hard-absence semantics) scores 0.91 (0.86 + 0.05 SUGG), clearing CF-001 at 0.90 on both consumer cases.

Late ignition timing / no-DTC ignition fault — POA_SIGNATURE chemistry (catch-all, variable gas signature) with elevated HC and no DTC requirement. Captures ignition-timing faults (knock-sensor fault causing late spark, failing coil producing weak spark below the misfire-detection threshold) that the ECU does not flag with a DTC. Low base_weight (0.42) prevents cannibalisation of other POA_SIGNATURE families: this rule fires at 0.57 (0.42 + 0.10 + 0.05) which beats no_fault but loses to any other family with a stronger signal. Known limitation: cannot flip case_036 (current winner CF-001 at 0.90) without raising base_weight above 0.75, which would cannibalise all POA_SIGNATURE cases — see progress_notes.
